because: Counterexample F4 (review 2026-10-05) held one point of the window; common::replay now proves the window arithmetic for all inputs (calibrated with the F4 fault). Narrowed after the review of #26 (counterexample: accept at T, another envelope of the sender at T + REPLAY_WINDOW_MS + 1 purges the nonce, a clock back at T accepts the original again): the proof is arithmetic, the stateful refusal holds only while the nonce is retained.
statement: REPLAY_WINDOW_MS covers MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_MS both ways, both bounds inclusive: for any timestamp and any two moments at which it is fresh, the window from the first covers the second (Kani: common::replay). So a replay is refused while its nonce is retained: until an envelope of the same sender arrives more than REPLAY_WINDOW_MS after it, and within one process lifetime. After such a purge, a clock that steps back to the first moment accepts the original again; no clock policy prevents that.
